Powering the UK
Mapping out the UK’s 
clean energy sector

This report analyses the ambitious private companies operating in 
the UK’s clean energy sector and the supporting mechanisms for 
growth. We’ve mapped out the landscape and have handpicked 
some of the most interesting companies by 5 metrics. 
Whether you work with or within the sector, we hope this report 
sheds some interesting light on this critical ecosystem.

The Climate Change Act 2008 committed the UK government to 
reduce greenhouse gas emissions by at least 80% of 1990 levels by 
2050. 
The government therefore has a vested interest in helping innovative 
clean energy  companies to grow and compete with the heavyweight 
industry incumbents that dominate the energy industry.

We use 8 criteria to identify high-growth 
and ambitious companies. Each of these 
are a sign of external validation that a 
business is either actively growing or 
creating ambitious growth plans. 
All companies featured in this report have 
met at least one of these growth triggers.
What do we mean by “ambitious”?
Equity investment
Accelerator attendance
Scaleups
MBO/MBI
Venture debt
Grant recipients
High-growth lists
Academic spinouts

There are 129 active, ambitious clean 
energy companies in the UK.
An additional 10 have exited the market, 
either through an IPO or an acquisition, 
and 27 are no longer trading.  
The sector is young, with 58% of 
companies at either seed or venture 
stage and only 11% at established. 
Comparing this to all ambitious 
companies across any sector these 
figures are 47% and 23% respectively. 
Stages of evolution

The UK’s clean energy companies are fairly 
well distributed across the country, with 
companies spread across England and a 
small hub in Scotland.
Indeed, Scotland is leading the way for 
carbon emission reduction in the UK, having 
met their commitment to a 42% reduction by 
2020 six years early. 
In May 2018 the Scottish government 
increased their target to a 90% reduction for 
all greenhouse gases by 2050 (compared to 
1990 levels).

73% of private clean energy companies have 
used equity funding to scale, significantly 
more than the rate across all ambitious 
companies: 53%. 
24% of clean energy companies are visible 
scaleups, double the rate of other companies 
across any sector. They are also twice as likely 
to be spinouts than the average. 
But only 10% of clean energy have attended 
accelerators, which is half the rate of all 
ambitious companies.

Methods of growth

The clean energy sector has a high 
concentration of grant recipients, with 38% 
of the active companies having received a 
large innovation grant. The rate across all 
ambitious companies is just 7.5%. 
As with most IP-heavy sectors, some clean 
energy companies are capital intensive and 
require significant time to reach market 
readiness. Patient capital therefore becomes 
an increasingly important support 
mechanism for the sector.
Grant statistics
NUMBER OF GRANTS AND AMOUNT GRANTED

Since 2011, clean energy companies have 
secured £739m in equity fundraising. Of this, 
£209m has never been publicly disclosed. 
2018 was a record year for the sector with 
£142m of equity invested. This was steered by 
clean energy supplier Bulb’s £60m round in 
June, backed by DST Global and Magnetar. 
The deal valued Bulb at £351m, and we 
suspect that the company will reach a billion 
dollar valuation over the next year or so. 
Fundraising statistics
NUMBER OF DEALS AND AMOUNT RAISED

Top investors
When looking at deal numbers alone, Scottish 
investors dominate the ranking of fund 
managers investing into clean energy 
companies in the UK, taking the top three 
places. 
Scottish Enterprise is the most prolific investor 
in the sector, completing 12 deals since 2011.
